title: Three Days and One Short Bowl
subtitle: 饮食与营养 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 饮食与营养（人与自我·生活与学习·饮食与营养）
meta: 主题语境：饮食与营养（人与自我·生活与学习·饮食与营养）　|　核心词汇：slice　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 slice 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1986 the cook ① cut the slice that no guest in the canteen would have counted, and he said the cutting was the whole of the day. The ② slice, meaning the piece itself and not the bowl, ran three days and stayed uncounted in the book; a slice, he said, is the only thing in a canteen that is judged by how long it is left uncounted.

Every ③ slice in that canteen had the same short bowl beside it, and the ④ slice at the far table, meaning the portion they kept for the children to share and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A slice, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to count; the cook said the counting is the part that fills three days.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the slice was the whole of the matter, meaning the share and not the piece. The ⑥ slice, meaning the share and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody counts; slice, he said, is either something you cut or the only word that means both a piece and a share. He said the share is the part they remember.

By 1991 the ⑦ slice had become a line in a menu, and the menu had become an argument about the short bowl. The ⑧ slice of the whole thing, the cook wrote in September, was one canteen and three days of counting; slice, he said, is either the portion at the far table or the reason you learned to count. He said the counting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ slice I remember is the piece counted in the menu, which closed in 1993 and is still counted as the quietest in the canteen. A ⑩ slice, my mother said in 1995, is the only piece that improves by being counted; every slice, she said, is a share that has agreed to look like a piece. She said the share was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 一片；薄片（指食堂里每一片旁边的那一片）
B. n. 一片；薄片（指那片一片本身，与小小的碗相对）
C. 固定搭配：cut the slice 切这一片一片
D. n. 一片；薄片（指留给孩子们分着吃的那一份）
E. n. 一片之事（抽象总称，指一处食堂的一片之事）
F. n. 一片；薄片（指菜单里写到、被清点的那一片）
G. n. 一片、一份（指一件事里人人都吃却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 一份（抽象总称，指人人都吃却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: cut the slice that no guest in the canteen would have counted
The slice, meaning the piece itself and not the bowl
the slice at the far table

answers.why: cut the slice 意为“切这一片一片”，1986 年那位厨子把食堂里没有一位客人肯清点的一片一片做了一遍。
slice 意为“一片；薄片”，指那片一片本身而不是小小的碗，它经过了三个日子而在簿子上没有被清点。
slice 意为“一片；薄片”，指食堂里每一片旁边的那一片，每一片旁边都有同一只小小的碗。
slice 意为“一片；薄片”，指最远那张桌角的留给孩子们分着吃的那一份，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
slice 意为“一片、一份”，指一件事里人人都吃却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这片一份就是那件事的全部。
slice 意为“一份”，指人人都吃却无人提起的那样东西而不是那片一片，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
slice 意为“一片；薄片”，指菜单里写到、被清点的那一片，到 1991 年这一片成了菜单里的一行。
slice 意为“一片之事”，厨子九月写道，整件事的一片之事是一处食堂和三个日子的清点。
slice 意为“一片；薄片”，我记得的是菜单里清点过的那一片，1993 年开完了，至今仍被说成食堂里最安静的一片。
slice 为抽象总称，母亲 1995 年说，一片是唯一会因为被好好清点而变得更好的一片。
